name: Adina Vălean - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing harmonised requirements in the internal market on transparency of interest representation carried out on behalf of third countries and amending Directive (EU) 2019/1937
part_text:
The report sets Parliament's position on a proposed EU law on transparency of lobbying done on behalf of third countries. It wants common minimum transparency rules across the EU, so lobbyists working for foreign governments or foreign bodies must register in a national register and disclose who they work for and roughly how much they are paid. It adds safeguards against stigmatising registered groups, keeps academic research and media work out of scope, and links national registers through a central public portal.

- **What changes:** Lobbyists for third countries must register, disclose their foreign clients and annual amounts, and face fines for breaking the rules.
- **Who it affects:** Companies, consultants, think tanks and civil society groups doing paid lobbying for foreign sponsors; not researchers, journalists or lawyers.
- **What happens next:** Parliament adopted this position; talks with EU governments follow before the law is final.
